description: A payment guide for a business paying or getting paid in Namibia, from one sentence, e.g. 'We are a Dutch logistics company starting truck operations out of Walvis Bay, paying drivers and suppliers in Namibia' or 'We pay traders in Namibia from South Africa every month'. Leads with paying and getting paid: the banks, fintechs, stablecoin platforms and crypto routes on record that can carry the payment, with speed and the forms of money each takes and pays out; what a payment really costs against the rate a currency site shows, worked from SwapEazi's own measurements; and the payment rules that decide whether money can move (exchange control, the Common Monetary Area, the documents a bank asks for before releasing a cross-border payment, limits). Then funding until contracts pay (institutions that publicly offer working-capital, asset or trade finance; information only, SwapEazi never lends, brokers or introduces for a fee); outside payments, who to see (each authority with its link; registration, tax and permits are not explained: use a tax or legal practitioner); documented payment pitfalls; what is not known and the next three actions with who approves what. Every fact with its source URL, date and evidence class (published, register, reported, not published). Information with sources, not legal, tax or financial advice. Paid per call: x402 (USDC on Base, price in the 402 body, USD 0.25) via params._meta["x402/payment"], or a paid router key as Bearer. The free summary is POST https://swapeazi.io/api/v1/pay-guide. The agent prepares; a person decides. SwapEazi never touches the money.
